atomicity.reason: One obligation (report overcurrent once the persistence timer reaches 100 ms), with the timer mechanics as its condition rather than a second requirement.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: threshold, direction, sample period, timer behaviour and output are all named in the requirement.

feasibility.reason: 1 ms sampling with an integer timer is routine on a shunt-based current path and matches the parent's stated sampling rate.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR owns the 100 ms persistence window as a monotonic timer starting above 350 A and resetting at or below it, so the supervisor sees an already-debounced condition; this requirement pins that timer.

unambiguity.reason: 'Until then the output reports no overcurrent condition' covers only the pre-trip phase; whether the reported condition clears when a later sample resets the timer, or latches, is not stated.
unambiguity.suggestion: State the post-trip behaviour explicitly, e.g. 'the reported condition shall clear when the timer is reset' or 'shall latch until the supervisor is reset'.

verifiability.reason: Threshold, sign convention, 1 ms sample period, increment and reset rules and the 100 ms deadline are all exact, so a sampled current sequence yields a single expected output.

summary: The most completely specified timer in the set - threshold, direction, sample period, accumulation and reset are all given; only the behaviour of the output after the timer has reset is left open.
